title: hybrid-token-window-collapse-and-kv-probe-scheduler
author: Riya Patel
description: Motivation: Small-chunk prefill reduces wasted tokens but increases kernel dispatch churn and KV cache thrash; large prefill reduces dispatch overhead but adds tail latency for short interactive requests. This PR introduces two coordinated techniques to improve throughput without regressing P95 latency for short requests: 1) Hybrid token window collapse: a scheduler-level coalescer that dynamically collapses adjacent micro-prefill requests from the same GPU worker into a controlled token window when the expected decode latency budget allows it. The window collapse heuristics consider sequence-length histograms, active KV cache occupancy, and per-worker kernel ramp cost so we avoid merging when it would increase peak memory/KV eviction risk. 2) KV probe scheduler: lightweight, speculative KV probes that run ahead of token handoffs to cold KV entries to reduce first-token decode stalls. Probes are size-limited and prioritized by recent key-access frequency and estimated prime benefit. Design: The collapse is implemented as a worker-side queue augmentation that tags micro-prefill entries with a collapseable token-range id; a window manager coalesces contiguous ranges based on a configurable latency budget and emits a combined prefill kernel call. The KV probe scheduler operates as a separate low-cost coroutine on each worker that issues non-blocking probe RPCs to the local KV shard with strict timeouts; results are merged into the worker KV cache and annotated with probe provenance to avoid double-eviction penalties. Implementation touches: runtime/scheduler/worker_queue.cc, runtime/scheduler/window_manager.cc, runtime/kernel/kernel_selector.cc, runtime/kv/kv_probe.cc, runtime/kv/kv_cache.cc, tests/bench/pipeline_hybrid_window.yaml, docs/perf/hybrid-window.md, examples/benchmarks/hybrid_window_runner.py, plus small changes to CI harness to surface new metrics. Backwards compatibility: All APIs remain internal to the runtime. The collapse window policy is off by default and guarded by a feature flag (ENV REDWOOD_ENABLE_HYBRID_WINDOW). Rollout plan: staged rollout behind the feature flag on canary pools for 48h, metrics review, then gradual ramp to all-serving nodes if no regressions. Benchmarks: Unit tests added. End-to-end benchmarks on c8-standard-16 show +18% throughput for mixed short/long workload and P95 latency change within +/-3% for 99% of runs; worst-case regression seen only at artificial adversarial load and was mitigated by lowering default collapse window size. Related work: complements speculative-chunking and prefetch reservoir strategies (see ENG-9876).

Add KV probe scheduler and merge probe results into worker KV cache
kernel selector tweaks to prefer fused-prefill kernels when windowed
address review feedback: tighten timeouts and add metrics
review_comments: Marco Chen: Can we avoid extra memory pressure when collapsing many long sequences? Please add a hard cap per-worker for merged token window sizes.
Riya Patel (author): Added a cap with eviction-aware heuristic and documented it; also added an integration test to validate memory bound behavior.
Ethan Alvarez: KV probe timeouts look aggressive; we saw probe RPCs piling up under high network jitter.
Riya Patel (author): Tightened probe timeouts, added exponential backoff for repeated probe failures and a probe-concurrency limiter per-shard.
Priya Rao: Please add instrumentation for probe hit/miss and collapse merge counts to the existing per-route trace.
Riya Patel (author): Added metrics (kv_probe_attempts, kv_probe_success, window_collapse_count) and trace annotations (probe_id, collapse_id).
ci_details: Integration pipeline_hybrid_window: pass after two reruns (one flaky timing test)
Performance smoke: pass with +18% mixed-workload throughput (canary)
release_notes: Introduce an opt-in hybrid token window collapse and KV probe scheduler to improve throughput on mixed-length workloads. Off by default; enabled via REDWOOD_ENABLE_HYBRID_WINDOW. Observability added for collapse/probe metrics. See docs/perf/hybrid-window.md for tuning guidance.
